title: GPU Spillover Orchestration and IaC Policy
author: Miguel Alvarez
content:
Summary

This document defines the architecture, Terraform/IaC patterns, CI/CD integration, and operational runbook for GPU spillover orchestration — the automated process that transparently redirects, shards, or degrades GPU workload placement when primary GPU pools reach capacity or violate placement SLOs. It codifies operator policies, safety nets, and network/egress considerations required by multi-account and multi-region deployments.

Goals

- Ensure customer-facing inference requests remain within latency SLOs by routing excess load to compatible fallback pools or quantized model variants.
- Preserve tenant isolation and egress billing clarity when spillover crosses cloud accounts or regions.
- Provide reproducible IaC patterns (Terraform modules + operator CRs) to deploy spillover logic consistently across accounts.
- Supply a concise oncall runbook for triage and rollback.

Scope and non-goals

- Scope: Redwood Dedicated clusters, Private on-prem gateways, cloud burst pools (AWS, GCP).
- Non-goals: Model-level quality tuning (model evals live in applied-ml-and-evals) and long-term cost optimization decisions — this doc focuses on orchestration and safety.

High-level design

1) Detection and policy decision path
   - Metrics sources: per-tenant queue depth, per-pool utilization (GPU %), token-per-second throughput, 95th/99th latency, preemption events.
   - Decision engine: a Kubernetes operator (spillover-operator) subscribes to metrics via Prometheus and applies policy CRs to decide: redirect, shard, or degrade.
   - Fallbacks: Compatible GPU pools (same architecture or quantized variant) or throttled CPU inference paths.

2) Routing and network considerations
   - Service mesh-aware routing: Envoy / Istio layer routes requests at the edge based on headers injected by the operator.
   - Cross-account egress: when routing to another cloud account, apply egress tags and a billing-annotation header for downstream metering.
   - Security: mutual TLS between control-plane components; IAM roles limited to assume/get-only permissions for cross-account routing.

3) IaC and Terraform modules (pattern)

   - Module responsibilities: define pool metadata, create spillover-operator Helm release, wire service accounts/roles, and publish pool capability descriptors (jsonnet or SSM parameter).

   - Recommended module inputs (table):

| input_name | type | description | example |
| pool_id | string | Unique pool identifier | gpu-pool-us-east-1a |
| region | string | Cloud region | us-east-1 |
| supported_models | list(string) | Model tags supported | ["gptx-13b:q8"] |
| max_concurrent_sessions | number | Soft concurrency limit pre-spill | 120 |
| egress_account_id | string | Account to route egress to on spill | 987654321012 |
| billing_tag | string | Cost center tag applied to spilled requests | team-search |

   - Minimal Terraform snippet (example)

   ```hcl
   module "gpu_pool_us_east" {
     source = "git::ssh://git.internal/repo/terraform-modules//gpu-pool"
     pool_id = "gpu-pool-us-east-1a"
     region = "us-east-1"
     supported_models = ["redwood/gptx-13b-q8"]
     max_concurrent_sessions = 120
     egress_account_id = "987654321012"
     billing_tag = "team-search"
   }
   ```

4) Operator CRD (behavioral knobs)

   - The spillover-operator CR supports the following fields (conceptual):
     - trigger_thresholds: latency_p95_ms, gpu_util_pct, queued_sessions
     - action_order: ["route_to_fallback", "shard_across_pools", "fallback_cpu_path"]
     - cooldown_window_secs: how long to wait after a corrective action before new checks
     - safety_cap: max % of tenant sessions allowed to spill to external accounts

   - Example YAML the operator consumes (condensed):

   ```yaml
   apiVersion: infra.redwood/v1
   kind: SpilloverPolicy
   metadata:
     name: search-tenant-spill-policy
   spec:
     triggerThresholds:
       latencyP95Ms: 400
       gpuUtilPct: 85
       queuedSessions: 30
     actionOrder:
       - route_to_fallback
       - shard_across_pools
     cooldownWindowSecs: 60
     safetyCapPct: 25
   ```

Implementation notes and edge cases

- Model compatibility matrix: when routing to a different quantized variant, the runtime must annotate provenance so client SDKs can expect lower fidelity and apply local post-filters.
- KV-cache affinity: prefer pools that can accept warm KV caches for sessions longer than 30s; otherwise fall back to cold-start tolerant pools.
- Preemption visibility: if the target pool has a history of preemption in the last 10m, exclude it from candidates.
- Egress chargeback: add header X-Redwood-Billing-Tag and a metric tag (billing_tag) to every spilled request for downstream invoice reconciliation.

CI/CD pattern and promotion flow

- Repo layout: infra/spillover/{modules,helm,operator,tests} with unit tests for Terraform and integration tests run in ephemeral sandbox environments.
- Pipelines:
  1. PR: terraform fmt -> tflint -> unit plan against mock backend -> helm lint -> operator unit tests.
  2. Merge to main: automated canary apply in dev account (ephemeral), smoke e2e against synthetic load generator, then promote via a controlled gate to staging and prod accounts.
- Canary safety gates: smoke tests must validate request path tagging, billing header present, and that no more than safetyCapPct of sessions were spilled.

Runbook: triage and manual rollback

- Pager triggers:
  - SLO breach: 5m sustained tenant 95th latency > configured threshold.
  - Unexpected spill volume: > 50% of a tenant sessions spilled for > 10m.

- Oncall steps (priority):
  1. Acknowledge incident and announce on #oncall-infra.
  2. Query operator status: kubectl -n infra get spilloverpolicy -o wide | grep <tenant-id>
  3. Inspect metrics: grafana dashboard "Spillover / Pool Utilization" and cross-check Prometheus query:
     - promql: sum(rate(gpu_sessions_total{pool=~"gpu-pool-.*"}[1m])) by (pool)
  4. If operator incorrectly routed to an external account, immediately set safetyCapPct=0 in the policy CR and apply:

     ```bash
     kubectl patch spilloverpolicy search-tenant-spill-policy --type merge -p '{"spec":{"safetyCapPct":0}}'
     ```

  5. If a Terraform-declared pool was misconfigured, run the terraform plan in the corresponding infra repo and revert the last change and trigger the pipeline to reapply the previous module version.
  6. If broad network egress spikes are observed, engage cloud-networking@redwood and trigger the egress quarantine (see Egress Quarantine procedure below).
  7. Post-incident: record in retro tracker and attach operator logs and Terraform plan diffs.

Egress Quarantine procedure (short)

- Use when cross-account egress causes unexpected billing or security alerts.
- Immediate actions:
  1. Mark the affected pool(s) with label x-redwood-egress=quarantine: kubectl label pool gpu-pool-us-east-1a x-redwood-egress=quarantine --overwrite
  2. Update spillover operator candidate list to exclude pools with that label (patch policy).
  3. Open a billing ticket and notify finance/CTI.

Operational telemetry and alert thresholds

- Must emit:
  - spill_events_total{tenant,from_pool,to_pool,reason}
  - spill_latency_ms
  - spill_ratio_pct (per-tenant)
  - pool_gpu_util_pct

- Suggested pager thresholds:
  - spill_ratio_pct > 30 for > 10m: P2
  - pool_gpu_util_pct > 95 for > 5m: P1
  - cross-account egress_bytes > 1TB/hour unexpected spike: P1

Ownership and rollout plan

- Owner: eng-infra / GPU Fleet (primary) with SRE (secondary) for oncall.
- Rollout plan:
  1. Deploy operator (v0.1) and module in dev account; run synthetic load tests.
  2. Promote to staging with limited tenants and enable detailed telemetry.
  3. Enable in prod for a pilot customer with 1-week observation window.

Appendices

A) Compatibility decision matrix (excerpt)

| Source pool | Accepts warm KV | Compatible quantized variants | Preemption history (10m) |
| gpu-pool-us-east-1a | yes | gptx-13b:q8, gptx-7b:q4 | no |
| gpu-pool-us-west-2b | no | gptx-13b:q8 | yes |

B) Example observability dashboard panels

- Pool utilization heatmap (by region/pool)
- Tenant spill ratio time series
- Cross-account egress bytes and billing-tag distribution

C) Helpful commands and queries

- List policies and status:
  kubectl -n infra get spilloverpolicy -o yaml | yq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, status: .status, lastAction: .status.lastAction}'
- Force a policy dry-run (dev only):
  curl -XPOST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $DEV_TOKEN' https://spill-operator.dev.internal/api/v1/dryrun -d '{"tenant":"tenant-123"}'
